r2_05_transition_bridge: R2-05 found descriptive frequency concentration in layer-local expert routing but explicitly declined to claim that frequency alone explains retention behaviour (R2-02's own evidence: LFU lost to Global-LRU at 4 GiB). R2-06 asks a DIFFERENT, complementary question: whether the ORDER of routing decisions carries information beyond that static frequency structure. A positive R2-06 finding (NMI > 0 for some layers) does not retroactively validate a frequency-only policy, and does not by itself establish that this transition structure is exploitable by any real policy -- that is a predictive-modelling question assigned to II-C, not measured here.

supported_now.claim: On the tested trace, the median per-layer same-layer normalized mutual information between consecutive token-to-token expert selections is 0.0989325510804687.
The strongest same-layer transition structure (highest NMI) is observed at layer 37; the weakest is at layer 45.
The fraction of layers with strictly positive NMI (i.e. the source expert carries SOME measurable information about the next same-layer target beyond marginal frequency) is 1.0.
The median per-layer self-transition lift (P(i->i) relative to expert i's own marginal probability) is 4.18503995784333, measured directly rather than assumed.
Previous same-layer expert selection state carries measurable information about subsequent same-layer routing state beyond marginal frequency, on this trace, for layers with NMI > 0.
